name: Dudhi na Muthiya
subtitle: steamed bottle-gourd and flour rolls, sliced and crisped in a sesame tempering

ingredients.note: keeps the crumb open rather than pasty

ingredients.qty: 6 tbsp: 3 into the dough, 3 for the tempering

prepNotes: Grate the dudhi and leave it in a bowl for 10 minutes, then squeeze it lightly and keep the juice. That liquid is all the water the dough needs.
Do not add plain water to the dough. If it is too stiff, add the reserved dudhi juice a spoon at a time.
The steamed rolls must cool completely before slicing, or they crumble. Steam them an hour ahead if you can.

steps.text: Mix the grated dudhi with the atta, besan, rava, ginger, green chilli, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, sugar, salt, lemon juice, baking soda and 3 tbsp oil.
Bring it together into a soft dough using only the reserved dudhi juice. It should be softer than chapati dough but hold a shape.
steps.tip: Work it quickly and lightly. A kneaded, over-worked muthiya dough steams up dense.

steps.text: Oil your palms and roll the dough into 3 logs about 5cm thick. Set them on a greased steamer plate.
Steam over boiling water for 22-25 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean and the surface is matte, not tacky.
Cool completely, at least 30 minutes, then cut into 1.5cm slices.
steps.tip: Slicing warm is the single most common failure. Wait.

steps.text: Heat the remaining 3 tbsp oil in a kadhai, crackle the mustard seeds, then add the sesame, asafoetida and curry leaves.
Lay the slices in and fry over medium heat, turning once, 4-5 minutes a side until the edges are golden and crisp.
steps.tip: Turn them once only and with a flat spatula; they break if you toss them.

steps.text: Scatter with coriander and coconut and serve hot with chai or plain yogurt.

storage: Steamed logs keep 3 days refrigerated, unsliced and wrapped. Slice and temper fresh. Muthiya reheated after tempering goes soft and oily.
